note: The two photographs of the Sears house this project reads. Both show one state of it: a smooth light ashlar street front two storeys over a raised basement under a slated mansard; at the north end a quoined pavilion carried up a storey past the main cornice, two paired lights in it, under a steep hipped roof with a cross finial; the door in the pavilion's south half under a pedimented hood on carved brackets, up a stoop between stone newels; south of it one window column and a gabled dormer in the mansard; at the south-west corner a one-storey bay, its north cheek canted, carrying a stone balcony of pierced panels; a deep stone cornice on blocks over a dentil course; two tall stacks, the south one broad; and a rock-faced, darker south flank. The interpretive panel at the site (Glessner House, c. 1980) draws the 1882 house the same way. The 1911 Sanborn sheet draws a one-storey projection north of the front's centre and no corner bay, so the 1902 Heun remodel may have changed the front: the photographs are evidence of their own (undated) state, weighed against the sheet in the match record.
